title: Coefficient passage for the explicit Frobenius point transport
statement: Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime l different from p and g_s the Frobenius point isomorphism [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Use the explicit integral, rational and algebraically closed transports [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], the point fibres [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and the rational and common-stage pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Supply the canonical object equalities hR: rational pullback objects equal the integral-model objects, hQ: common-stage pullback objects equal the explicit Frobenius objects, and hF: the chosen algebraically closed fibre objects equal their stage-pair objects. These are equalities of the already specified constructions, not additional mathematical hypotheses. Then (1) the explicit algebraically closed transport is natural for every common-stage morphism, with hF and hQ inserted at the endpoints, and (2) every finite coefficient extension E to L intertwines explicit rational transport with the specified fibre scalar isomorphism and inverse pullback scalar comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension, lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. The orientations and all object-equality insertions are the two displayed equations in the attached Lean statement. This result concerns coefficient passage only, not linearity or sigma/finite/integral/rational naturality.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.3) and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; explicit coefficient-normalization and common-stage argument from steps 3-4 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural, written by an agent.

proof.text: Identify the module restriction transformation of [lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural] at g_s with the finite and integral sigma of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], using their values on every section. Restriction along the inverse ULift ring equivalence identifies the completed section functors. Localization of this equality, and naturality of the specified kappa from [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-natural], identify the integral transport with the normalized pointTransport family.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.3) and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; explicit coefficient-normalization and common-stage argument from steps 3-4 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural, written by an agent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-point-automorphism-transport-scalar-extension] to this family. Use pointFibreRationalDownIso and the coefficient-size descent counit of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] to identify its rational components with frobeniusPointTransportRational. Naturality of the counit cancels size descent. The pure-tensor normalizations of the fibre scalar isomorphism and the integral normalization of rationalPullbackScalarComparison identify the outer comparisons. Cancel normalization isomorphisms and use faithfulness of the carrier lift. Insert hR, the supplied rational object equality, to obtain the second displayed equation in the Lean statement.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.3) and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; explicit coefficient-normalization and common-stage argument from steps 3-4 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural, written by an agent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-point-transformation-coefficient-descent] to the integral family for all finite coefficient subfields. Step 1 supplies naturality and Step 2 supplies scalar compatibility. Its rational normalization agrees with the preceding identification. Its common-stage normalization therefore identifies its components with the images of the explicit rational transport at each object stage, precisely frobeniusPointTransportQbar. Descended naturality gives the first equation after inserting hF and hQ. Proof irrelevance shows that the choice of equality proofs is immaterial.

lean.statement:
theorem frobeniusPointTransport_coefficient_passage
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (hR : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
      (N : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l E (Spec (.of D.k))),
      letI := frobeniusPointPrimeInvertible D l hl
      (rationalDerivedPullback l E (frobeniusPointIso D).hom).obj N =
        frobeniusPointRationalPullbackObj D l hl E N)
    (hQ : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra ℚ_[l] Ω] [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] Ω]
      (A : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω (Spec (.of D.k))),
      letI := frobeniusPointPrimeInvertible D l hl
      (commonStageDerivedPullback l Ω (frobeniusPointIso D).hom).obj A =
        frobeniusPointQbarPullbackObj D l hl Ω A)
    (hF : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra ℚ_[l] Ω] [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] Ω]
      (A : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω (Spec (.of D.k))),
      (pointQbarFibre D l hl Ω).obj A = pointQbarFibreObj D l hl Ω A) :
    (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra ℚ_[l] Ω]
      [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] Ω]
      (A B : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω
        (Spec (.of D.k)))
      (u : A ⟶ B),
      letI : ∀ x : Spec (.of D.k), Invertible (l : (Spec (.of D.k)).residueField x) :=
        fun x => frobeniusPointPrimeInvertible D l hl x
      (eqToHom (hF Ω A).symm ≫
          (pointQbarFibre D l hl Ω).map u ≫
          eqToHom (hF Ω B)) ≫
          frobeniusPointTransportQbar D l hl Ω B =
        frobeniusPointTransportQbar D l hl Ω A ≫
          (eqToHom (congrArg (pointQbarFibreObj D l hl Ω)
              (hQ Ω A).symm) ≫
            eqToHom (hF Ω
              ((commonStageDerivedPullback l Ω (frobeniusPointIso D).hom).obj A)).symm ≫
            (pointQbarFibre D l hl Ω).map
              ((commonStageDerivedPullback l Ω (frobeniusPointIso D).hom).map u) ≫
            eqToHom (hF Ω
              ((commonStageDerivedPullback l Ω (frobeniusPointIso D).hom).obj B)) ≫
            eqToHom (congrArg (pointQbarFibreObj D l hl Ω)
              (hQ Ω B)))) ∧
    (∀ (E' L : Type u) [Field E'] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E']
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E'] [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L]
      [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L] (ι : E' →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L)
      (K : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l E' (Spec (.of D.k))),
      letI : ∀ x : Spec (.of D.k), Invertible (l : (Spec (.of D.k)).residueField x) :=
        fun x => frobeniusPointPrimeInvertible D l hl x
      (pointRationalFibreScalarIso D l hl E' L ι).inv.app K ≫
          frobeniusPointTransportRational D l hl L
            ((sfRationalScalarExtension l E' (Spec (.of D.k)) 0
              (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) L ι).obj K) ≫
          (pointRationalFibre D l hl L).map
            (eqToHom (hR L
              ((sfRationalScalarExtension l E' (Spec (.of D.k)) 0
                (Nat.Prime.ne_zero (Fact.out : l.Prime)) L ι).obj K)).symm) ≫
          (pointRationalFibre D l hl L).map
            ((rationalPullbackScalarComparison l E' L ι
              (frobeniusPointIso D).hom).inv.app K) ≫
          (pointRationalFibreScalarIso D l hl E' L ι).hom.app
            ((rationalDerivedPullback l E' (frobeniusPointIso D).hom).obj K) =
        (DerivedCategory.pointFdScalarExtension ι.toRingHom).map
          (frobeniusPointTransportRational D l hl E' K) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.pointFdScalarExtension ι.toRingHom).map
            ((pointRationalFibre D l hl E').map
              (eqToHom (hR E' K).symm)))
